title: Route checks by job kind per ci-routing 3.2, with athena.toml
summary: Add a routing function in athena-core mapping a plan's class_of_work to which checks run, which are skipped, and where the result comes from (reused CI result via item 4 `resolve`, or local), following the section 3.2 table. Unlike the failed attempt, athena.toml is listed as a deliverable and named in a criterion, because the per-kind routing rules are expressed there. Audience: the Athena maintainer and ci-routing.md reviewers.

defaults_applied.how: All code in Rust in athena-core.
Routing tests plus cargo test, clippy, fmt must pass.
Criteria run tests that exercise each kind and the SHA-mismatch and red-CI paths.
Criteria check the checks that run per kind, not that the file exists.
One focused change on routing only.
Routing rules live in athena.toml and code, enforced by tests.
Doc update claims no measured speedup.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Section 3.2 is the source of truth: code/tests run fmt, clippy, test; docs/design/study skip fmt and clippy but always run test; config never skips; build is as code plus the workflow's own run and never reuses a prior result.
Missing or unknown kind takes the config row (all three checks, none skipped), per section 7.

athena.toml is edited to carry the per-kind routing (for example a per-kind skip rule beside the existing [[capabilities.change.checks]] entries), and CheckSpec in capability.rs is extended only if the schema needs a new field.
Routing consults item 4's `resolve` with the candidate SHA: a CI result for another SHA is ignored and falls back to local; a red CI result fails without a local rerun.
No speedup is measured; the doc update says so.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core routing`: for each kind (code, tests, docs, design, config, build, study, other) the routed checks and skips match the section 3.2 table (docs, design and study skip fmt/clippy but always run test; config never skips; build adds the workflow's own run and never reuses a prior result).
Run `cargo test -p athena-core routing`: a missing or unrecognised job kind gets the config row (fmt, clippy, test, none skipped), per section 7.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test shows the routed path calls `resolve` with the candidate SHA; a CI result for another SHA is ignored and falls back to a local run; a red CI result fails and does not rerun locally.

Run `cargo test` (including a test that loads the committed athena.toml with the schema in the tree): athena.toml parses, and representative jobs of each kind run the checks section 3.2 assigns to that kind.
athena.toml is modified to express the per-kind routing, and `git diff` shows the change; if CheckSpec needed new fields, the schema change is in the same commit.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both pass; `cargo test` passes in full.
docs/design/ci-routing.md section 10 item 5 states what was built and what is not done (for example no speedup measured), without claiming a measured improvement; CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
The routing is called from the job run or verifier input path (run.rs / verify.rs), not only defined; a reader can find the call site that selects checks by the plan's kind.

out_of_scope: Measuring speedup or running the section 9 baseline
departures: Larger change than typical (new module, config and schema edits, call-site wiring), so cost and time are above the reference.
